reason: I want to follow how blood is filtered through a nephron, as the first goal suggests.

reaction: The distinction between small substances and most proteins makes the filtering step clearer.
reason: The selective transporters seem like the next step in returning useful substances to the blood.
expectation: I expect some useful dissolved substances to move from the tubule back into the blood.

reaction: Seeing glucose recovered clarifies why filtering is followed by selective recovery.
reason: The water-permeable tubule appears to be the next step in following the filtered sample.

reason: Urinary drainage appears to continue the sample's path toward urine.

reaction: The path from filtered blood to urine is clear, though the last step was predictable.
reason: The ureters connect the kidneys to the bladder, so they are a useful next fitting.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidney pair, leaving a connection for the bladder.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also needs fitting, but I chose to connect the tubes from the kidneys first.

reaction: The fitting was predictable and clearly follows the drainage route.
reason: The bladder is the only available combination and completes the visible drainage connections.
expectation: I expect the bladder to attach to the ureters, forming connected urinary organs.

effect: The kidneys, ureters and bladder are connected, so the urinary organs can now be added to the body.
reaction: The explanation makes the drainage route clear, although the fitting was predictable.
reason: This is the only available combination and should complete the remaining goal.

effect: The kidneys are now connected to circulation, and the urinary organs are connected to the body. Both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The final connection brings the chapter together, though it was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Recovering useful substances after filtration was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidneys filter blood and then return needed materials, including glucose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder was clear but repetitive after the urine had already been shown following that route.

surprise.text: I learned that healthy kidneys normally recover almost all filtered glucose.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt purposeless. The organ fittings were straightforward, though the available combinations guided the choices.

continue.text: I would continue if the next chapter offers another clear connection between body systems. The filtration and recovery sequence held my interest, though the final fittings were less engaging.
